itemListElement.name: Moving a piano: what drives cost and risk (upright vs grand, stairs, floors)

acceptedAnswer.text: Third-party surveys put a straightforward local move in the low hundreds: ConsumerAffairs found average local flat rates of $275 for an upright and $450 for a grand (1), and Angi's 2026 data puts the typical professional move between $200 and $1,000 (2). Stairs, weight and distance move the figure. We publish no per-type price list — the piano is surveyed and quoted inside the one flat rate in writing.

mainEntity.name: How much does it cost to move a piano?

acceptedAnswer.text: General movers move pianos routinely; what separates a good outcome is whether the piano is surveyed and planned as a piece, not discovered on move day. ConsumerAffairs carries the cautionary version: a crew that arrived not knowing a baby grand — let alone its staircase — was part of the job (1). We move pianos as white-glove pieces, with the piece named in the Detailed Project form before the day.

mainEntity.name: Can regular movers move a piano, or do I need a specialist?

acceptedAnswer.text: A few front steps usually change nothing in published market pricing, but a full flight does: about $100 added on average for an upper floor in the ConsumerAffairs survey (1), and roughly $40 to $100 per flight in Angi's data (2). On our side there is no separate stair charge — the stairs at both addresses are part of the survey that sets the one flat rate in writing (6).

By size: a baby grand typically runs 500 to 800 lbs, a medium grand 700 to 900 lbs, and a concert grand 900 to 1,300 lbs — a Steinway Model D is about 990 lbs (6). Individual instruments vary by 100 lbs or more within a type, which is why movers ask about the specific piano, not just the type. Weight is what sets the crew size and the handling plan.

mainEntity.name: How much does a grand piano weigh?

acceptedAnswer.text: Federal rules give interstate moves two liability options: full value protection, and released value at 60 cents per pound per article (1, 3). Released value on a 500 lb baby grand pays $300 — far under the instrument's worth — and anything worth more than $100 per pound counts as an item of extraordinary value to declare in writing (3). We publish no valuation figures of our own; declare the piece and its importance when the job is scoped.

mainEntity.name: Will my piano be covered if it is damaged?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Movers move pianos; technicians tune them, and tuning is not part of our service (6). The Piano Technicians Guild's guidance is that it is the climate change around a move, not the move itself, that drifts a piano out of tune — so let the instrument settle into its new room for a week or two, then book a technician for the tuning (4).
